Every cloud-AI action in Dhaga costs **credits**. `/app/settings` → **Credits**
is the page that tells you how many you have left, where the rest went, and
what you did to spend them.

![The Credits tab in Dhaga settings: a "Credits this month" card showing 33 of 85 credits left with a used-bar, a reset date, and a Monthly allowance / Credits added for you / Total breakdown, above a "Where your credits went" card listing deep research, card scans, Ask Dhaga, notes, briefs, drafts, quick adds, and free watchlist scans with their counts and credit costs](/docs/guide/credits.png)

## How many are left

The first card is the headline: **credits remaining out of your total for the
month**, a bar showing how much of it you have used, and the date the counter
resets. Allowances do not roll over — a fresh month starts from the full
number.

Every plan has an allowance, including the free one: a **free account gets 10
credits a month**. That is ten card scans, or five scans and five notes, or five
questions to Ask Dhaga — enough to keep capturing with AI, not enough to lean on
it all month.

If your plan has no monthly ceiling, the card says **Unlimited** and shows what
you have used so far instead of a number left.

If something has been *added* to your allowance, the card breaks it down rather
than just showing a bigger number:

- **Monthly allowance** — what your plan (or this instance's configuration)
  includes.
- **Promotion this month** — replaces the line above when whoever runs the
  instance is running a promotional month.
- **Credits added for you** — a one-off grant, e.g. after something went wrong
  on their side. Grants are always *added on top*; they never rewrite what you
  spent.

## Where your credits went

The second card is the breakdown for the current month: one row per kind of
action, how many of them you ran, and what they cost. **The rows add up to the
total** — that is the same number your monthly cap is measured against, so
nothing is counted twice or quietly left out.

Credits are charged per **action**, not per model call — a card scan that takes
two round-trips behind the scenes is still one scan:

| Action | Credits |
|---|---|
| Card scan | 1 |
| Quick add (pasted text or a signature) | 1 |
| Note (text) | 1 |
| Follow-up draft | 1 |
| Ask Dhaga (a question) | 2 |
| Pre-meeting brief | 2 |
| Deep research (enrich from the web) | 20 |
| Watchlist scan (nightly) | Free |

A **photo note** costs 2 — reading the image and extracting from the resulting
text happen as two separate actions.

**Deep research** is the expensive one on purpose: it pays for live web
searches on top of the model, and it is the only action whose real cost is
dominated by something other than Dhaga's own tokens.

**Watchlist scans are free.** They appear in the breakdown marked *Free* rather
than being hidden, so a month of nightly scanning is visible and accounted for
without costing you anything. You never asked for any individual scan — how
many people you can watch is what limits them instead.

**Credits aren't the only gate**

Deep research costs more than a free month holds, and **deep research and
pre-meeting briefs are Pro-and-up features** anyway — having credits left over
doesn't unlock them. What a free allowance realistically buys is card scans,
notes, quick add, follow-up drafts and questions to Ask Dhaga.

## Recent activity

The last card is a plain list of your AI actions — *"Card scan · 1 credit · 2
hours ago"* — newest first. It starts by showing your most recent actions, and
a **Load more** button at the bottom fetches further back, so you can page all
the way through your entire usage history, not just what you did this week.
It is not limited to the current month either, so opening the page on the 1st
still shows you what you last did.

**This page is yours alone**

Everything here is derived from your own usage records. Whoever runs the
instance has a separate [admin
screen](/docs/self-hosting#instance-wide-ai-credit-controls-appadminai-credits-hostedee)
for setting allowances and granting credits — it never shows them what you
asked or what you captured.

## Running out

When the month's credits are gone, you find out **before** you click: the AI
buttons are greyed out, with the reason sitting next to them — *"You're out of
AI credits this month — all 10 used. They reset on the 1st."* — and a **See
credits** link back to this page. Nothing fails silently, and nothing is charged
for an action you didn't get.

Greyed out until the counter resets: **Extract contact** on the paste tab,
**Scan card**, **Ask Dhaga**, **Brief me**, **Draft follow-up**, and **Enrich
from public web**.

Everything that doesn't spend credits keeps working exactly as before — manual
capture and editing, adding a fact or a follow-up by hand, search by name, the
graph, import, export, and voice dictation (which runs on your own device).
Adding photos to a card-scan tray still works too; only the **Scan** button
itself is greyed.

**Notes are deliberately never greyed out**, typed or photo — writing something
down must not depend on having credits. What you had already typed is never
thrown away either: save a note with an empty balance and it still saves — you
just get told what didn't happen: *"Note saved.
You're out of AI credits this month, so facts weren't extracted."* (a photo note
says *"Photo note saved…"*). You can add facts by hand, or re-run extraction on
that note once the counter resets.

Seeing *"No monthly AI credits on this plan — upgrade to enable AI actions"*
instead? That is a cap of **0**, which only happens when whoever runs the
instance has deliberately set your allowance there. It is not what a free
account normally looks like.

Self-hosting? `DHAGA_AI_MONTHLY_CAP` seeds your instance's monthly allowance —
it applies until an admin sets a number in the app, and from then on the stored
number is the one that counts. See [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).

---

# Calendar & reminders

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/calendar

See every follow-up and upcoming birthday on a full-screen calendar — drag to reschedule, schedule date-less ones from the tray, and stay nudged by the notification bell and opt-in reminder emails.

**`/app/calendar`** lays every open follow-up out on a full-screen calendar, so
you can see what's coming instead of scrolling a list. Dated follow-ups land on
the grid; date-less ones wait in a tray you drag onto it. It's an extra way to
work the same follow-ups you already set — nothing new to maintain.

![The follow-ups calendar](/docs/guide/calendar.png)

## Month and list views

Two views share a toolbar at the top — **month** for the grid and **list** for a
week-at-a-glance agenda — with **prev / next / today** to move around. The
calendar opens on the month grid on desktop and the list view on a phone,
whichever reads better on the screen you're on.

## Reschedule by dragging

Pick up any follow-up and drop it on another day to move its due date. The
change saves as soon as you let go — if anything goes wrong it snaps back and
tells you. No dialog, no form: just drag it where it belongs.

## The unscheduled tray

Follow-ups you logged without a due date don't disappear — they gather in an
**Unscheduled** tray above the calendar, each as a chip with the contact's name
and what you meant to do. Drag a chip onto a day to give it a date; it leaves the
tray and takes its place on the grid. Collapse the tray with its header when you
want it out of the way.

## Open a follow-up's details

Click any item — on the grid or in the tray — to open its details. From there
you can:

- **Open contact** — jump straight to the person's page.
- **Mark done** — close the follow-up out.
- **Dismiss** — clear it without marking it done.

![A follow-up's details dialog opened from the calendar](/docs/guide/calendar-event.png)

## Birthdays and anniversaries

Any **important date** you've saved on a contact — a birthday, a work
anniversary, the day you met — shows up here too, on the day it comes round each
year. They sit on the grid as soft amber all-day entries reading
*"Priya — Birthday"*, with a quieter second line for the age or count where the
saved date includes a year.

They behave differently from follow-ups, on purpose:

- **They aren't draggable and they can't be marked done.** A birthday isn't a
  task you complete — it's a fact about a person. Drag one and it snaps straight
  back.
- **You edit them on the person.** Click one and Dhaga opens the contact; the
  date lives under **More details → Important dates**, where a calendar picker
  (with a year dropdown, so a 1974 birth year is two clicks) sets it. Change it
  there and the calendar follows.
- **They're worked out on the fly**, never stored as separate reminders. Fix a
  date or forget a person and nothing is left behind to clean up.

Dates you imported from Google Contacts or a `.vcf` sometimes arrive as plain
text — *December 9*, or a day and month with no year. Dhaga keeps those exactly
as they came and still works out when they next fall; it never quietly rewrites a
date you didn't type.

How far ahead a date counts as "upcoming" is yours to set, under **Suggestions**
in [Settings](/docs/guide/settings) — 7 days by default.

## Your connected calendar, alongside

By default a connected calendar tells Dhaga only when you're **busy** — blocks
of time, no titles, no attendees — and Dhaga never writes to it. That stays true
unless you say otherwise.

If you **upgrade** a connection in [Settings](/docs/guide/settings), two things
change for that calendar and nothing else:

- **Its events show up here**, next to your follow-ups and styled differently so
  you can always tell which is which. They're read-only in Dhaga — to change one,
  change it in the calendar it came from. Only a window around today is fetched,
  so events far in the past or future won't appear.
- **Your follow-ups get written out** to a separate calendar Dhaga creates,
  called **Dhaga**. Never your main calendar — so you can hide it, or delete it
  outright, without touching anything of your own. Reschedule a follow-up and its
  event moves; mark it **done** or **dismiss** it and the event is removed.

Both are per-connection and per-account: upgrading one calendar leaves any other
connection exactly as it was. You can switch the write-out off on its own, from
Settings, and keep the connection.

**Event details stay on your screen**

Titles, locations and guests from a connected calendar are only ever displayed.
Dhaga doesn't store them, doesn't log them, and doesn't send them to an AI model.

## Staying reminded

You don't have to keep the calendar open to stay on top of things:

- The **bell** in the top nav opens **Notifications** — one short list holding
  three things: follow-ups **due today** or **overdue**, birthdays and
  anniversaries coming up, and word that a background job has finished (a note
  you added has turned into facts, an enrichment has landed). Mark a follow-up
  **done** right there, dismiss a notification with its **×**, or jump to the
  full calendar or your follow-ups list. When it's empty, you're all caught up.
  The **count on the bell** is deliberately narrow — things to act on *now*: what's
  overdue or due today, anything unread, and a date only once it's actually
  arrived. A birthday next week is in the list without nagging you.
- **`/app/follow-ups`** gains an **Upcoming dates** block below your open
  follow-ups, showing who's next and how far off. It's simply absent when nothing
  is coming.
- Turn on the **daily reminder email** to get a morning nudge whenever follow-ups
  are waiting — it now reaches you while there's still time to act, covering
  anything due in the next few days rather than only what's already late.
- Turn on the separate **birthday and anniversary email** to hear about a saved
  date before it lands. You'll get at most two per occasion: one when it comes
  into view, one on the day.

Both emails are opt-in and both start off — flip them on under **Suggestions** in
[Settings](/docs/guide/settings), where you can also set your **time zone** so a
day starts and ends where you are.

**The calendar is an extra view, not a replacement**

Your **Home** briefing and the **`/app/follow-ups`** list still show the same
follow-ups — the calendar just adds a spatial, drag-to-reschedule way to see
them. Use whichever fits the moment.

---

# Capturing people

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/capturing-people

Add a person to your graph from pasted text, a card photo, voice, your webcam, or a file — with a review step that confirms the fields before saving.

Capture is one click from anywhere. An **Add** button in the app nav opens the
capture dialog on **every** `/app` screen — the fastest path in. The same
capture also lives in the **capture dock** at the bottom of every screen and on
the dedicated **`/app/quick-add`** page, which additionally lets you attach the
new person to an existing event (below). All run the same extraction, keep the
original input as a **receipt**, and meter AI usage per account. A card scan or
a paste-to-contact costs **1 credit**, and the free tier includes **10 AI
credits a month** — ten card scans, say, or five scans and five notes. Run out
and the app stays fully usable for manual capture. See
[AI credits](/docs/guide/ai-credits).

## Quick-add modes

The capture panel opens on the **Manual** tab — the fastest, no-AI path, and the
one that keeps working when you're out of credits, or on a self-hosted instance
with no API key. Three
pills across the top switch between **Manual**, **Paste text**, and **Card
photo**.

- **Manual** (the default) — type the person in by hand with no AI. Manual has
  its own sub-tabs to add a **person**, a **relationship** between two people, or
  a **fact / follow-up**. See [Adding someone manually](#adding-someone-manually)
  below.

![Dhaga manual add-person form with fields for name, jobs, emails, phones, and links](/docs/guide/add-person.png)

Switch to an AI capture mode for however else you captured the person:

- **Paste text** — drop in an email signature, the text off a business card, or a
  LinkedIn intro, and Dhaga pulls out the name, title, company, and contact
  methods. On this tab (outside the home dock) a **Voice** mic sits under the
  box: tap it and describe who you met; the dictation streams live into the text
  and is extracted the same way. With Dhaga Voice the transcript comes back as
  tappable word-chips — tap a mis-heard word to fix it, and Dhaga learns that
  spelling for next time.

![Dhaga quick-add in paste-text mode, ready to accept an email signature or card text](/docs/guide/quick-add-paste.png)

**Voice needs WebGPU**

Dhaga Voice dictation runs entirely on-device, so it needs **WebGPU** — available
today in desktop Chrome and Edge. On iOS Safari and other browsers without WebGPU,
Dhaga detects this up front and shows a clean "voice isn't supported on this
device — type it in instead" message rather than failing mid-recording. Manual
entry is always available.

- **Card photo** — take or upload a photo of a business card. Dhaga runs OCR and
  also reads a LinkedIn QR code if one is on the card. You're not limited to one
  shot: add several photos of the same card or leaflet — front and back, or
  multiple pages — in a tray where you can reorder, crop, or remove any of them
  before scanning. On desktop you can also shoot straight from a live webcam,
  capturing multiple frames in one sitting. Every image you add merges into a
  **single** contact, and each photo is kept as its own source receipt.

The capture dock at the bottom of the screen adds two more shortcuts:

- **Camera** — shoot one or several frames straight from your webcam. **Done**
  drops them into the card-photo tray, so you can crop, reorder, or remove any
  of them before pressing Scan.
- **Upload** — attach an image or file you already have.

![Dhaga quick-add in card-photo mode with a "Take or choose card photos" drop area (front, back, or multiple pages all merge into one contact), a Use live camera button, and the Voice / Camera / Upload capture dock](/docs/guide/quick-add-capture.png)

**AI extraction needs a key**

The card scan, voice, and text extraction run through Claude. On a self-hosted
instance without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, capture falls back to simpler heuristic
parsing. See [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting) for the env var.

**Prefer your phone?**

You can also forward a contact card, note, or photo straight to Dhaga on
WhatsApp or Telegram — no app to install. See
[Messaging capture](/docs/guide/messaging-capture).

## Review, disambiguate, and save

Extraction never saves silently. A **review dialog** shows the fields it pulled
so you can correct them before the person lands in your graph:

1. Check the name, title, company, emails, phones, and links.
2. If the details look like someone you already have, Dhaga flags the match so
   you can merge into the existing contact instead of creating a duplicate.
3. Optionally **attach the person to an event** right from the review dialog —
   handy when you're clearing a stack of cards from one conference. See
   [Groups & events](/docs/guide/groups-and-events).
4. Save.

## Adding someone manually

Manual is the **default** tab — the capture panel opens on it, so typing a person
in by hand (no AI, no API key) is the zero-click path. Its sub-tabs let you add a
**person**, record a **relationship** between two people you already have, or log
a **fact / follow-up** against a contact. Switch to **Paste text** or **Card
photo** whenever you'd rather have Dhaga extract from captured input, or go
straight to **`/app/people/new`** for the full person form.

![The Manual hub with its Person, Relationship, and Fact / follow-up sub-tabs](/docs/guide/quick-add-manual.png)

The person form keeps **Experience** and **Education** as two separate sections:

- **Experience** — roles with a title, company, dates, and a **relationship
  type** (employment, internship, founder, board member, advisor, volunteer).
- **Education** — schooling with an **institution**, **degree / programme**,
  **field of study**, years, and a **currently studying** toggle. Education is
  stored as a "studied at" affiliation, so schools become nodes in your
  [graph](/docs/guide/exploring-the-graph) just like employers.

Add as many of each as you need, along with several labelled emails and phones
and links, then save.

![The manual person form's Experience and Education sections — Education showing Institution, Degree / programme, Field of study, year fields, a "Currently studying here" toggle, and a relationship-type selector](/docs/guide/add-person-education.png)

---

# Companies

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/companies

View, create, rename, delete, and merge the companies in your graph — with duplicate detection — from a dedicated management page.

Companies are first-class nodes in your graph — the thread between everyone who
works, or worked, somewhere. Manage them from their own page.

Open **`/app/companies`** — it's in the nav **More** menu. The table lists every
company with its **contact count**, so you can see at a glance where your
network clusters.

![The Companies page: a table of companies with domain, sector, and contact-count columns, per-row actions, and a New company button](/docs/guide/companies-list.png)

## Create, rename, delete

- **Create** a company inline from the page — handy when you want it to exist
  before attaching anyone.
- **Rename** one from its row actions.
- **Delete** a company when it's noise. Deleting **detaches** its people and
  their job history — everyone's **positions are kept, only the employer link is
  cleared** — then removes the company. **It never deletes contacts.** Your
  people stay; they just no longer point at that company.

You can select several companies at once to delete or merge them together.

## Merge companies

Two entries for the same employer — "Acme" and "Acme Inc." — creep in easily
across imports. Select two or more and **Merge**:

1. **Pick the survivor.**
2. **Resolve conflicts** on the single-value fields — **name**, **domain**, and
   **sector** — wherever the entries disagree.
3. All **contacts**, **positions**, and **relationship edges** from the others
   are **re-pointed** onto the survivor, and the merged-away companies are
   deleted.

Like a contact merge, it's one atomic step.

**Merging can't be undone**

The merged-away companies are deleted with no undo. Their people, jobs, and
edges move to the survivor first, so nothing is lost — but pick the survivor
deliberately.

## Aliases

Companies pick up other names — a prior name, an acronym, an acquisition. Dhaga
tracks these as **aliases**, so a later import that still uses an old name
resolves to the right company instead of creating a duplicate.

- **Merging records them automatically.** When you merge companies, each
  merged-away name (and any aliases it already had) becomes an alias of the
  survivor.
- **Add your own.** Open a company's edit dialog and use **Also known as** to
  add, rename, or remove aliases — changes save as you make them.
- **See them all** on **`/app/companies/aliases`** — the **Aliases** link in the
  Companies page header — which lists every alias next to its company, each
  editable or removable in place.

![The Company aliases page: a list of alternate names, each shown next to the company it resolves to, with inline edit and remove controls](/docs/guide/companies-aliases.png)

## Find duplicate companies

**`/app/companies/duplicates`** groups companies that are probably the same by
their **normalized name** — ignoring case, punctuation, and common legal
suffixes (Inc, Ltd, LLC, GmbH, Pvt, and the like) — so "Acme, Inc." and
"Acme LLC" land in the same cluster. Each has a **Review & merge** shortcut into
the merge dialog.

![The Duplicate companies page: Acme, Acme LLC, and Acme, Inc. grouped into one cluster normalised to "acme", with contact counts and a Review & merge button](/docs/guide/companies-duplicates.png)

Companies appear on the [graph](/docs/guide/exploring-the-graph) too, as the
nodes tying colleagues together.

---

# Confirmations

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/confirmations

A unified inbox for the doubts AI raises — when extraction is ambiguous it defers to a confirmation instead of guessing, and nothing touches your graph until you confirm.

When Dhaga is *sure* about what it extracted, it just writes it. When it isn't —
a name that could be two different people, a web-sourced fact that might not be
the right person — it doesn't guess. It parks the doubt as a **confirmation** and
lets you decide. **AI proposes, code disposes:** the model only ever writes a
confirmation row; your graph is changed by a deterministic resolver, and only
once you say yes.

The **`/app/confirmations`** inbox is where those doubts collect. **Confirmations**
sits in the left nav with a small amber count pill when any are waiting.

![The Confirmations inbox at /app/confirmations (a top-nav item with a count badge) with pending questions grouped by type — "Links to confirm", each offering candidate contacts to pick from plus a search box and confirm/dismiss actions](/docs/guide/confirmations.png)

## The four kinds of doubt

Each confirmation is one of four types, phrased as a plain question:

- **Entity link** — an ambiguous mention. You wrote "I know Ajay" and you have two
  Ajays; Dhaga asks which contact the relationship should point at rather than
  picking one.
- **Subject resolution** — the classic *"who is _he_?"*. A note refers to someone
  by pronoun or a bare first name, and Dhaga asks which contact is the subject
  before wiring up the relationship.
- **Enrichment match** — a fact pulled from the public web that might not really
  be this person. Confirming clears the *unverified* badge; dismissing removes the
  fact.
- **Supplement** — a batch of newly-extracted facts and edges ready to fold into
  an existing contact, once you okay the addition.

## Confirm or dismiss

Every row shows the question and — where relevant — the candidates to choose from.

- **Confirm** and the deterministic resolver applies the exact proposed action:
  it links the edge to the contact you picked, verifies the fact, or folds in the
  supplement. The action is stored on the confirmation, never re-derived from
  free text, so what you approve is exactly what runs.
- **Dismiss** and the doubt is discarded, changing nothing.

**Nothing changes until you confirm**

A pending confirmation has written **no** edge, fact, or relationship to your
graph. That's the point — ambiguous extraction waits for you instead of leaving
you to clean up a wrong guess later.

## Who is this note about?

Unlike the four above, this question never lands in the inbox — it appears
**inline in quick-add**, the moment you capture the note. When a note you type
reads as being about someone but Dhaga can't be sure who, the card pops up right
there in the capture panel and you answer it on the spot, before anything is
saved. (See
[Capture a note from quick-add](/docs/guide/notes-and-facts#capture-a-note-from-quick-add)
for how a typed note gets recognised in the first place.)

The card shows the **note text** up top so you have the full context, then gives
you two ways to place it:

- **Pick a person** — contacts whose name matches the note's subject appear as
  chips; tap one and the note attaches there, its facts and relationships
  extracted as usual. You can also search for anyone else if the right person
  wasn't surfaced.
- **Create a new one** — a name field, prefilled with the name from the note,
  lets you say *"no — this is a different Anchit, add them"*. Dhaga creates a
  fresh contact and attaches the note to it. When nobody matched at all, the card
  leads with this.

![Confirming who a note is about](/docs/guide/note-capture-confirm.png)

**Dismiss** drops the captured note without writing anything — the same rule as
every other confirmation.

## Where they surface

- **Home** shows a **To confirm** tile listing the first few pending questions,
  with a link straight through to the inbox. It only appears when something is
  waiting — it's an alert, not a fixture.
- **The nav badge** carries the pending count so you can see there's something to
  review without opening the page.

## Get them by email

If you'd rather be nudged, turn on the **Confirmations digest** under **Settings →
Suggestions**. It's **off by default**; once on, a summary of your pending
confirmations goes out on the daily job. Like the other digests, it needs email
configured on your server — see [Settings](/docs/guide/settings) and
[Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).

---

# Enrich from the web

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/enrich-from-web

Search the public web for a person's footprint on demand — always user-triggered, cited on every finding, and saved as a note you can delete.

Sometimes you want more context on a person than your own notes hold. The
**Enrich from public web ✦** button on a person's page fetches it — on demand,
never automatically.

![A person's profile with the amber Enrich from public web button and its caption explaining that findings are cited, saved as a note, and fully deletable](/docs/guide/person-facts-enrich.png)

## What it does

Press the button and Dhaga searches the public web for that person's footprint.
As the caption on the button says, it *"searches the public web for their
footprint — cited, saved as a note, fully deletable."* Concretely:

1. Findings come back **cited** — every claim links to where it was found.
2. They're saved as a **normal note** on the person, just like one you'd write
   yourself.
3. That note can, in turn, yield **facts** (each with its receipt).
4. You can **delete** the note — and its derived facts tombstone with it — at
   any time.

The search plus extraction takes 20–60 seconds and runs **in the background**:
the progress pill above the Facts section tracks it, it keeps running if you
leave the page, and it finishes with a short confirmation of what was added. Go
elsewhere in the meantime and the result finds you through the
[**bell**](/docs/guide/calendar#staying-reminded) in the top nav — including when
it turns up nothing, or fails.

Enrichment is a **Pro-and-up feature**, and the most expensive action in Dhaga
at **20 [credits](/docs/guide/ai-credits)** — it pays for live web searches on
top of the model. A free account's monthly allowance doesn't stretch to one, and
wouldn't unlock the button even if it did.

## Privacy

Enrichment is **always user-triggered**. Dhaga never reaches out to the public
web about a contact on its own or in the background — you press the button, for
one person, each time. That keeps enrichment consistent with the rest of the
product: no silent data collection.

**Requires a configured search provider**

Enrichment runs against a web-search backend, which a self-hosted instance has
to supply. Set `SEARCH_PROVIDER` and its key, or implement your own — see
[Add a search provider](/docs/extending/search-provider). Without one
configured, the Enrich button has nothing to call.

---

# Custom entities

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/entities

Model the non-person things that connect your people — gyms, schools, projects — as custom entity nodes with their own types.

Not everything in your network is a person. The gym where you know three people,
the school two contacts both attended, the project a handful of them worked on —
these are **entities**, and they connect people just like relationships do.

Manage them at **`/app/entities`**. Entities are grouped by **type**, and you
can define your own **custom node types** to match how you actually think about
your network.

![The entities page listing custom non-person nodes such as gyms, schools, and projects, grouped by type](/docs/guide/entities-list.png)

Entities appear on the [graph](/docs/guide/exploring-the-graph) alongside
people, so a shared gym or project becomes a visible thread between the people
attached to it. Use the Layers panel there to show or hide entity types when the
canvas gets busy.

## Custom relationship types

The **Add relationship** dialog (on any person, company, event, or entity page)
comes with built-in relationship types — *father of*, *works at*, *studied
at*, and so on — but you can also create your own, like *introduced to* or
*potential collaboration with*, right there while adding one.

Manage the ones you've created from **`/app/entities`** too, next to entity
types — **Manage relationship types** lists each with how many relationships
use it, and lets you rename it or delete it (deleting is blocked while any
relationship still uses it, so you never lose data by accident).

For a quick fix, you don't have to leave the Add relationship dialog: click
the pencil next to any of your custom types in the picker to rename it inline.

---

# Exploring the graph

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/exploring-the-graph

Your whole network on one canvas — find warm-path intros, open a node's edges in a side panel, toggle layers, and zoom or reset the view.

**`/app/graph`** renders your entire network on a single canvas. Every person
and connection you've captured is one node in a graph you can pan, zoom, and
interrogate.

![The Dhaga graph canvas showing the full network settled into a layout, with the warm-path panel in the top-left corner](/docs/guide/graph-overview.png)

## Find a warm path

The **Warm path** finder answers "how do I get introduced to this person?"
Enter a target and Dhaga renders the **intro chains** that connect you to them
through people you both know — for example *You → Bhavna Costa → Aarav Bose*.

![The warm-path panel listing three intro chains from you to a target person through mutual connections](/docs/guide/graph-warm-path.png)

## Inspect a node

Click any node to open its **side panel**. It shows that person's edges — split
into **incoming** and **outgoing** — and lets you:

- **Add a relationship** to another person — search your graph, or add a new
  person on the spot if they aren't in it yet.
- **Open** their full profile page.
- **Isolate their circle** to focus on just their immediate connections.

![The graph with a node selected, its side panel showing incoming and outgoing edge counts, and the focused node's circle isolated](/docs/guide/graph-node-panel.png)

## Reading the edges

Edges are **directional**, and hovering a node makes the direction obvious: its
**outgoing** edges — the ones where it's the subject — thicken into solid amber
with a clear arrowhead, while edges merely **pointing at it** stay softer and
thinner. So *Ajay → parent of → Anchit* reads at a glance.

Employment and schooling both draw an edge from the person to the organisation:

- A current employer is the person's primary **"works at"** edge.
- Past employers render as their own **"worked at"** edges — every role in a
  person's history shows, not just the current one.
- Education renders as **"studied at"** (or "attended").

![A hovered person node on the graph with its outgoing edges thickened into solid amber arrows and its incoming edges rendered softer and thinner](/docs/guide/graph-edge-direction.png)

## Layers and controls

- The **Layers** panel toggles which node types and circles are drawn, so you
  can declutter a dense graph.
- **Zoom**, **fit**, and **reset** controls frame the view — fit to see
  everything, reset to return to the default layout.

Non-person nodes like gyms or projects show up here too — see
[Custom entities](/docs/guide/entities).

---

# Groups & events

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/groups-and-events

Group the people you met at a gathering into an event, add them in a row from the roster, email a digest, and let Dhaga suggest groups it spots.

An **event** in Dhaga is any gathering or group — a conference, a dinner, a
team. The people you met there stay grouped, so months later you can still
answer "who did I meet at that dinner?" The rule is simple: **one event per
event.**

## Create an event

Go to **`/app/events`**. The inline create form takes a **name**, an **emoji**,
and a **colour** so each group is recognisable at a glance. Below it, the events
table lists every group with its emoji, tags, people count, and start date.

![The events page with an inline create-event form showing an emoji and colour-swatch picker, above a table of existing events](/docs/guide/events-list.png)

## Add people to it

Open an event to see its **roster**. Use the **Add people** search box to attach
several people in a row without leaving the page — type a name, pick, repeat.

![An event detail page showing its people roster and an Add people search box](/docs/guide/event-detail.png)

You can also add a person to an event **from their own profile** — **Add to
group** sits in the sticky sidebar next to Edit and View in graph, a handy
shortcut when you're looking at someone and remember where you met them. Groups
show as their own row on the profile, kept separate from that person's tags —
which have their own **Add tag** control, letting you search tags you've used
before or create a new one on the spot.

## Manage and share

From an event you can:

- **Email a digest** of the attendees to yourself.
- **Rename, restyle** (emoji/colour), or **retag** the group.
- **Merge** two events that turned out to be the same gathering.

**Digests need email configured**

The attendee digest sends over email, which a self-hosted instance wires up
with `RESEND_API_KEY` and friends — see the
[Self-host env var reference](/docs/self-hosting#self-host-env-var-reference).

## Suggested groups

Home surfaces **suggested groups** — clusters of people Dhaga noticed belong
together — so you can turn a pattern it spotted into a real event with one tap.

---

# Importing contacts

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/importing-contacts

Bring an existing address book into Dhaga — from a .vcf or CSV file, a one-click Google or Outlook connection, or the contacts already on your phone.

Already have an address book somewhere? Import it instead of re-typing. Dhaga
takes it three ways: a **file** you export (works everywhere, no setup), a
**one-click connect** to Google or Outlook, and **on-device import** in the
mobile app. Existing people are matched and skipped, and every imported field
keeps a **receipt** so you can trace where it came from — a permanent note on
the contact, not something you can edit away.

Open **`/app/import`** (it lands you on **Settings → Import**), or scroll to the
**Import contacts** section on `/app/settings`.

![Dhaga's Import contacts screen: a drop area for a .vcf or CSV file, a Choose file button, and collapsible per-source export instructions](/docs/guide/import-contacts.png)

## From a file (.vcf or CSV)

Drop a `.vcf` (vCard) or `.csv` onto the import area, or click **Choose file**.
The file is **parsed entirely in your browser** — nothing is uploaded until you
pick who to keep. You then get a **review list** to select rows, and only the
selected contacts are saved.

The screen has collapsible **"How to export from…"** steps for each source. In
short:

- **iPhone / iCloud** — on a computer, sign in to **iCloud.com → Contacts**,
  press **⌘A / Ctrl+A** to select everyone, then the gear (bottom-left) →
  **Export vCard**. (On the phone you can share a single contact as `.vcf`, but
  iCloud.com exports everyone at once.)
- **Android** — **Contacts app → Settings → Export → Export to .vcf file**, then
  move it to your computer.
- **Google** — **contacts.google.com → Export** and choose **vCard** or
  **Google CSV** (both work here).
- **LinkedIn** — click **Get contacts from LinkedIn** on the import screen to open
  LinkedIn's **"Get a copy of your data"** export page in a new tab (or go there
  yourself via **My Network → Connections → Manage synced contacts**). LinkedIn
  emails you the archive — usually about a day later — then you upload the
  `Connections.csv` here.
- **Outlook** — export contacts as CSV from Outlook and drop the file in.

**Dhaga reminds you to finish a LinkedIn import**

LinkedIn doesn't hand you the file on the spot — it emails the archive about a
day later, which is easy to forget. After you click **Get contacts from
LinkedIn**, Dhaga sends a short "did your export arrive? upload it here" email on
days 1, 3, 6, and 7, then stops — and stops sooner the moment you import your
LinkedIn contacts. The reminders only go out on instances with email configured;
a self-host without email set up simply skips them.

**Big address books**

Very large files (100k+ contacts, tens of MB) will warn you and can be slow —
split the `.vcf` into a few smaller files if it drags.

## One-click: Connect Google or Outlook

When the instance is configured for it, a **Connect an account** row appears
above the file drop with **Connect Google Contacts** and/or **Connect
Outlook / Hotmail** buttons. Clicking one sends you to that provider's own
consent screen — you're granting **your own account**, read-only, and you can
disconnect any time. On return, your contacts come straight into the same
review-and-select list as a file import.

- **Google** covers Google Contacts.
- **Outlook** covers Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live, and Microsoft 365.

**These buttons only show when configured**

The connectors need a one-time operator setup (OAuth credentials). If you don't
see them, the instance hasn't wired them up — the file import above covers every
source in the meantime. Operators: see [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting) and the
repo's `docs/CONTACT_IMPORT_SETUP.md` for the Google Cloud / Azure steps.

## No Apple / iCloud connector

There's no "Connect iCloud" button — Apple provides no contacts API. For
Apple/iCloud contacts, use the **`.vcf` export** from iCloud.com described above;
it brings in everyone at once.

## On your phone (mobile app)

The mobile app can import the contacts **already on the device**. Open the
**Import contacts** screen, grant the **Contacts** permission when asked (iOS and
Android each show a native prompt; if you decline, the screen offers an **Open
Settings** shortcut), then pick who to bring in. It uses the same API key you set
up on the mobile Setup screen — no extra configuration.

**Needs a native build**

On-device import ships as code but needs a native app build to appear (it can't
arrive via an over-the-air JS update or plain Expo Go), and is pending on-device
testing.

Once people are in, add [notes and facts](/docs/guide/notes-and-facts),
[enrich them from the web](/docs/guide/enrich-from-web), or group them into
[events](/docs/guide/groups-and-events).

---

# Connect an AI assistant (MCP)

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/mcp

Dhaga speaks the Model Context Protocol, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any other MCP client can read your network and write back to it — ten tools, no AI credits for the reading half.

Ask Dhaga answers questions *inside* Dhaga. **MCP** is the other direction:
point an assistant you already use at your graph and let it ask on its own,
in the middle of whatever else you were doing.

- *"Who did I meet at the conference last month?"*
- *"Save the recruiter who referred me, and remind me to follow up Friday."*
- *"Which employers haven't got back to me?"*

The endpoint is **`/api/mcp`** on your instance. Any client that speaks the
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can connect to it —
Dhaga doesn't ship a per-client integration, because the client discovers the
tools, their inputs and their descriptions at connect time.

## Connecting a client

There are two ways in, and both reach the same tools. Which one you use depends
on the client, not on what you're allowed to do.

### As a connector (log in, no keys)

Dhaga is its own **OAuth 2.1 authorization server**, so a client like claude.ai
or ChatGPT can add it the way it adds any other connector: you paste the URL,
Dhaga shows you a normal login and a consent screen, and the client gets a token
of its own. Nothing is copied around by hand, and you can only ever grant access
to your own account.

Add a custom connector in the client and give it one thing — the endpoint,
`https://your-dhaga-host/api/mcp`.

Everything else is negotiated. The client fetches Dhaga's discovery documents
(`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`), registers itself, and sends you to
log in.

### With a personal access token

For local clients — Claude Code, Cursor, anything running on your own machine —
the simpler path is the **API key you already have**. It's the same personal
access token the mobile app uses, created under **Settings › Account › API
keys** (see [Settings](/docs/guide/settings)).

Claude Code, in one line:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http dhaga https://your-dhaga-host/api/mcp \
  --header "x-api-key: YOUR_TOKEN"
```

Any client that takes a raw HTTP MCP server config wants the same two things —
the URL and the header:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dhaga": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://your-dhaga-host/api/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "YOUR_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

A token is as good as your account, so treat it like a password: it goes in the
client's config, not in a note, a repo, or a chat message. Revoke it in
Settings and every client holding it stops working immediately.

### Clients that only speak stdio

Some MCP clients still launch a local process and talk over stdin/stdout rather
than HTTP. Bridge those with
[`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote), which runs as the local
process and forwards to the endpoint:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dhaga": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://your-dhaga-host/api/mcp",
        "--header", "x-api-key:YOUR_TOKEN"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

That's a community bridge, not something Dhaga ships — prefer a direct HTTP
connection wherever the client offers one.

## What the assistant can read

Six read tools, and none of them spend AI credits:

- **`dhaga_search`** — hybrid keyword + semantic search across contacts and
  note text. It returns the people **plus the snippets that matched**, so the
  assistant can tell you *why* someone came back rather than asserting it.
  Capped at 20 results.
- **`dhaga_list_contacts`** — browse with filters (name, company, tag, starred)
  and pagination, up to 100 per page.
- **`dhaga_get_contact`** — one person in full: details, job history, the facts
  extracted from their notes (each with the `sourceNoteId` receipt it came
  from), up to 25 recent notes, and their open follow-ups.
- **`dhaga_list_follow_ups`** — everything you're on the hook for, across the
  whole network, soonest-due first.
- **`dhaga_find_warm_path`** — up to three introduction paths to a person or
  company, through people you already know.
- **`dhaga_list_upcoming_dates`** — birthdays and anniversaries in the next N
  days (30 by default, 365 at most), resolved in your own timezone.

Dhaga tells the connected model, at connect time, to treat your graph as the
only source of truth about who you know — and to say so plainly when the answer
isn't there rather than filling the gap from what it happens to know about a
similarly-named public figure.

## What it can write

Four write tools, all **additive**:

- **`dhaga_add_note`** — attach a note to a contact.
- **`dhaga_create_contact`** — save a person. Only a name is required; title,
  company, emails, phones, links, location and a first note are all optional.
- **`dhaga_create_follow_up`** — open a reminder (what to do, plus an optional
  due date).
- **`dhaga_close_follow_up`** — mark one **done** or **dismissed**.

A note written by an assistant goes through exactly the same path as one you
type in the app: it queues background extraction, and every fact or follow-up
derived from it keeps a `source_note_id` receipt. Delete the note later and its
derived facts go with it, as always.

## What it deliberately cannot do

There is **no delete, no merge, no bulk action, no export, and no admin tool**,
and that is a decision rather than a gap.

**Why the write half stops where it does**

Deleting a contact in Dhaga cascades — the person, their notes, the facts
extracted from them, their graph edges and their embeddings all go. That is
right when *you* click it and unrecoverable when a confused or prompt-injected
client does. So the irreversible operations stay in the app, where a human is
looking at them.

`dhaga_close_follow_up` is the one thing that might read like a deletion and
isn't: it changes a follow-up's status, and the follow-up stays on the contact.

## What it costs

**Reading your graph costs no AI credits at all.** There is deliberately no
"ask Dhaga" tool in the MCP surface — the client on the other end is already a
model, so it gets raw retrieval with receipts and does its own reasoning. You
are not paying Dhaga to think on top of something that already thinks.

The one exception is notes. **`dhaga_add_note`**, and `dhaga_create_contact`
when you give it a `note`, queue the normal background extraction — **1
credit**, exactly as if you had written the note in the app. If you're out of
credits for the month the note is still saved; only the extraction is skipped,
and the assistant is told so rather than left to assume it worked. See [AI
credits](/docs/guide/ai-credits).

There's also a plain request limit — **60 tool calls a minute**, per person. An
assistant working through a question makes several calls a turn and won't
notice it; a client stuck in a retry loop will, and that's the point.

## For self-hosters

MCP is **pure AGPL core**. It imports nothing from `packages/ee`, needs no
cloud tier, and your instance serves the identical `/api/mcp` endpoint — a
self-hosted Dhaga is a first-class MCP server, not a degraded one.

**Set BETTER_AUTH_URL correctly**

The OAuth issuer is derived from `BETTER_AUTH_URL`. If it doesn't match the URL
clients actually reach your instance on, the tokens Dhaga issues will be
rejected by the client that asked for them. The personal-access-token path is
unaffected by this — it's a plain header.

**Dynamic Client Registration today, CIMD later**

The 2026-07-28 MCP spec deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favour of
**Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD)**. Dhaga's authorization server is
better-auth's `mcp` plugin, and better-auth 1.6 implements DCR but does not
advertise CIMD yet — so DCR is what's live at `/api/auth/mcp/register`, and it
works with the clients shipping today. CIMD support lands here when better-auth
ships it.

---

# Bulk actions & merging

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/merging-and-bulk-actions

Act on many people at once from the People table — merge duplicates into one record, add a company, tag, star, or forget in a batch — and let Dhaga surface likely duplicates for you.

Your **People** list isn't only for browsing. Select several people and act on
them in one go, or fold two records of the same person into a single one.

## Select people

On **`/app/people`**, every row has a checkbox, and the header checkbox selects
everyone on the current page. Your selection **sticks as you page through** the
table, so you can gather people across several pages before acting. The moment
one person is selected, a **bulk-action bar** appears.

![The People table with three rows selected and the bulk-action bar above it showing Merge, Add to company, Tag, Star, Unstar, and Delete](/docs/guide/people-bulk-actions.png)

## Act on the selection

With people selected, the bar offers:

- **Merge** — combine two or more records of the same person into one (needs at
  least two selected). See below.
- **Add to company** — attach everyone to a company at once; pick an existing
  one or create it inline.
- **Change relationship** — relabel how the selected people relate to a company
  — studied at, worked at, interned at, board member of, and so on. Only the
  label changes; nobody moves companies. See
  [Relabel relationships in bulk](#relabel-relationships-in-bulk) below.
- **Tag** — add or remove a tag across the whole selection.
- **Star** / **Unstar** — flag or unflag people for your Saved list.
- **Delete** — forget the selected people. This cascades — their notes, facts,
  edges, and embeddings go too — exactly like "forget this person" on a single
  profile.

## Relabel relationships in bulk

Phone and address-book imports often land everyone at a place as "works at" —
including the classmates you studied with and the professors who taught you.
**Change relationship** fixes a whole batch in one pass:

1. Select the people and click **Change relationship**.
2. Choose **which company** the label applies to — **their current company**
   (each person's own), or **a specific company** you pick.
3. Choose the new relationship — **studied at**, **worked at**, **interned at**,
   **board member of**, and so on, or create your own type.
4. Apply.

Only the affiliation *label* changes — nobody is moved to a different company.
So students relabelled to "studied at" and the professors left as "works at"
still cluster on the same university node in your
[graph](/docs/guide/exploring-the-graph).

![The Change relationship dialog: a "Which company" choice of Their current company or A specific company, and a Relationship picker offering studied at, worked at, interned at, and more](/docs/guide/people-change-relationship.png)

## Merge duplicate contacts

Met the same person twice — a card scan and a LinkedIn import, say — and now
they're two records? **Merge** folds them into one:

1. Select the records and click **Merge** (or start from **Find duplicates**,
   below).
2. **Pick the survivor** — the record everything else folds into.
3. **Resolve conflicts.** Where records disagree on a single-value field —
   **name**, **nickname**, or **location** — you choose which value wins. Fields
   where they already agree don't ask.
4. Everything that can hold more than one value is **combined** onto the
   survivor: emails, phones, links, addresses, important dates, custom fields,
   tags, jobs, notes, facts, and relationship edges. Nothing is dropped.

The other records are then **permanently deleted**. It all happens in a single
step — either the whole merge lands or nothing changes.

**Merging can't be undone**

The records you merge away are hard-deleted, with no undo — the same model as
"forget this person." Their data lives on in the survivor, but the separate
records are gone. Make sure you've picked the right survivor first.

## Find duplicates

You don't have to spot duplicates yourself. The **Find duplicates** link in the
People page header opens **`/app/people/duplicates`**, which groups likely
duplicates it notices — by a **shared email**, a **shared phone**, or a
**similar name** — into clusters. Each cluster has a **Review & merge** button
that opens the merge dialog prefilled with that group, so cleaning up is two
clicks.

![The Find duplicates page listing contact clusters grouped by a shared email, each cluster showing the matching people with a Review & merge button](/docs/guide/people-duplicates.png)

Companies have the same tools — view, merge, and dedupe them on the
[Companies](/docs/guide/companies) page.

---

# Messaging capture (WhatsApp & Telegram)

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/messaging-capture

Forward a contact card, a note, or a photo to Dhaga's WhatsApp or Telegram bot, reply DONE, and Dhaga saves the person into your graph — capture from your phone with nothing to install.

Dhaga can capture people straight from a chat you already have open. **Forward
a contact card, a note, or a photo** to the Dhaga bot on **WhatsApp** or
**Telegram**, reply **`DONE`**, and Dhaga creates and tags the contact, keeps
every forwarded message as a **receipt**, and replies with a summary. It's the
fastest way to capture from your phone without any app install — hand someone's
card straight into your graph while you're still standing at the booth.

This is a **core, fully self-hostable** feature — it needs no cloud tier. Setting
up the bot (the webhook, the API keys) is a one-time admin job covered in
[Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting); this page is about *using* it once a channel
is connected.

## Connecting your chat

There's one bot per deployment, so Dhaga has to know which account a chat
belongs to before it saves anything.

1. Open **Settings → Messaging** (`/app/settings`).
2. Generate a **link token** — a short, single-use code that expires in a few
   minutes.
3. Send that code to the bot as a message. Dhaga links your chat to your
   account and replies to confirm.

From then on, anything you forward from that chat lands in *your* graph. A chat
that isn't linked yet gets a friendly nudge back explaining how to link it.

**Self-hosting for one person**

On a single-owner self-hosted instance, an unlinked chat falls back to the
owner automatically (set by `DHAGA_OWNER_EMAIL`), so you can start forwarding
before wiring up per-user linking.

## What you can forward

- **Contact card** — a shared vCard is imported from its own fields (name,
  numbers, org), never re-read as text, so nothing is lost in translation. A
  card for someone a note already mentioned fills that person in instead of
  duplicating them.
- **Text** — a message you type or forward becomes a note, and Dhaga
  auto-extracts facts from it, each with a receipt back to the message.
- **Photo** — a business card or badge is scanned into a contact; a photo that
  *isn't* a card (a whiteboard, a poster, a conference schedule) is read as text
  and kept as a note. Send a caption with it and the caption becomes a note on
  that person.
- **Location** — kept as a note on the current contact.

Anything else — a **voice note** (see below), a video, a document, a sticker, an
empty message — gets a reply telling you so. Nothing is ever dropped in silence:
if an item can't be saved, either the bot answers straight away or the batch
summary lists what it skipped and why.

## How a batch works

Forwarding is **positional**, so the order you send things in is what Dhaga
acts on — no guessing:

- A **contact card or photo** sets the *current contact*.
- **Text that follows** attaches to that contact as notes and facts.
- A leading **text with no card** establishes the contact on its own, the same
  way pasted text does in [quick-add](/docs/guide/capturing-people).
- Forward **several cards** in one batch and you get several contacts — each one
  collects the messages sent after it.

## When Dhaga isn't sure who you mean

If a forwarded note could be about more than one person in your graph, Dhaga
asks **in the chat** rather than guessing:

```
🤔 That note could be about more than one "Ajay". Which one did you mean?
1. Ajay Shrivastava (STPI)
2. Ajay Kumar (Infosys)
```

Reply with the **number**, the **name**, or **`new`** for a new person. If you
reply with something else entirely, the question is dropped, the note is saved
under a new person so it can't be lost (merge them later if that's a duplicate),
and your new message is handled normally. A question expires after an hour.

A note that matches exactly one person is attached to them silently — no
question, and no duplicate contact.

## Closing a batch

You never have to remember to finish — a batch is saved three ways, and nothing
is ever lost:

1. **Reply `DONE`** (or `finish`, `end`, `/done`) to save immediately.
2. **Start a new forward** and any earlier open batch is saved first.
3. **Walk away** — an idle batch auto-saves after about 15 minutes of quiet
   (self-hosters can tune this with `DHAGA_MESSAGING_IDLE_MINUTES`).

When a batch is saved, the bot replies with a summary of who and what it stored
so you can open Dhaga and review.

**Voice notes aren't supported yet**

Forward a voice note and the bot replies *"Voice notes aren't supported yet —
coming soon! For now please type it, send a photo, or forward a contact."* — it
is never quietly swallowed. Server-side transcription is a pluggable gateway
that ships with **no provider**, and the refusal is gated on that gateway: the
day a provider is configured, voice notes start being transcribed and attached
like any other note, with no further change. (This is separate from **Dhaga
Voice**, the on-device dictation in web
[quick-add](/docs/guide/capturing-people) — that one does transcribe.)

## More channels later

WhatsApp and Telegram ship today, but the messaging layer is provider-agnostic:
it mirrors Dhaga's [LLM and search gateways](/docs/extending), so a new channel
is a self-contained plug-in with no changes to the capture flow above. If you
self-host, see [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting) for the per-channel setup.

---

Next, see how forwarded notes turn into searchable facts in
[Notes & facts](/docs/guide/notes-and-facts), or bring in an existing address
book from [Importing contacts](/docs/guide/importing-contacts).

---

# Notes & facts

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/notes-and-facts

Add notes to a person by typing, by voice, or by photo; Dhaga extracts structured facts automatically (or add facts and follow-ups by hand — no AI needed), keeps a receipt on each, and cascades deletions.

Everything you know about a person lives on their profile at
**`/app/people/[id]`** — their jobs, contact methods, location, relationships,
and, below that, their **notes and facts**.

![The top of a person's profile showing their jobs, email, location, and relationships](/docs/guide/person-detail.png)

## Add a note

In the **Notes** box on a person's page, either type what you remember or tap
the mic and just talk — voice notes are transcribed for you. The box hints as
much: *"Type — or tap the mic and just talk. Facts get extracted
automatically."* With Dhaga Voice, the transcript comes back as tappable
word-chips so you can fix any mis-heard word — doing so teaches Dhaga that
spelling for next time. Or [photograph it](#add-a-note-from-a-photo) — the
third way into the same box.

![A person's profile showing the Facts section with two extracted facts, the Enrich from public web button, and the Notes box with Add note and Voice note buttons](/docs/guide/person-facts-enrich.png)

## Add a note from a photo

Some things are quicker to photograph than to write down: a whiteboard after a
session, a conference poster, a page of handwritten notes, a receipt from the
dinner, the badge someone was wearing.

Tap **Photo note** in the same Notes box and pick or shoot the photo. Dhaga
reads the text out of it and **that text becomes the note** — so it is searchable,
it shows in the person's timeline, and it goes through exactly the same
extraction as anything you type: facts, follow-ups and relationships, each with
a receipt pointing back at this note.

- **Several photos, one note.** Add up to six — pages of the same handout, or
  two halves of a whiteboard. They are read in tray order, so reorder them with
  the arrows if you shot them out of sequence, and crop out anything that isn't
  the subject.
- **Add your own line too.** Anything you type in the box is kept above the
  transcription, as your framing of why the photo matters.
- **The photo is kept as the receipt.** It appears under **Photos** on the
  person's page, alongside any scanned cards, unless you have turned
  [photo storage off in Settings](/docs/guide/settings) — in which case only the
  transcription is kept. Deleting the note deletes its photos with it.

Reading a photo is a cloud-AI action, so it costs credits like any other — 2 in
total, since reading the image and extracting facts from it are two actions.
With no credits left, or on an instance with no AI configured, type the note
instead — a photo alone has nothing to save.

## Capture a note from quick-add

You don't have to be on someone's page to note something about them. Type a
free-text note into [quick-add](/docs/guide/capturing-people) — *"Met Anchit,
discussed the Q3 pilot"* — and Dhaga recognises it as a note **about a person
you already have**, not a brand-new contact to create.

It matches the name against your contacts and attaches the note to that person's
timeline, where its facts and relationships get extracted just like any note you
add on their page.

- **One clear match** and it attaches straight away — *"Added a note to
  Anchit"*, nothing to click.
- **Unsure** — several people could be the *Anchit* you meant, or nobody matches
  at all — and Dhaga asks first instead of guessing, showing a
  [who-is-this-about card](/docs/guide/confirmations#who-is-this-note-about) right
  in quick-add so you can pick the right person or add a new one on the spot.

## Facts get extracted automatically

When you save a note *and you have AI credits left this month*, Dhaga extracts
structured **facts** from it — for example a personal detail or an intent
("wants an intro to a designer"). Each fact is tagged by kind (**PERSONAL**,
**INTENT**, and so on).

Every extracted fact carries a **receipt**: the source note it came from, shown
as *"FROM NOTE, 23/7/2026"*. This is a core principle — no AI-derived fact
exists without a traceable source you can open and verify.

Extraction runs **in the background**, and the note is saved the moment you
press **Add note** — so you never have to sit and watch it. A small pill above
the Facts section reports progress (*"Extracting facts…"*), and it keeps running
if you navigate away or close the tab: the facts are written server-side
regardless of who is watching. While you're on the page, the pill turns into a
short confirmation of what landed — *"Extraction finished — 4 facts and 1
follow-up added."* — and clears itself. If a run fails, the pill says so and
offers **Retry**.

If you've already moved on, the finished run reaches you through the
[**bell**](/docs/guide/calendar#staying-reminded) in the top nav instead —
*"Extracted 4 facts and 1 follow-up from your note about Priya"* — and clicking
it takes you back to the person. Runs that failed, or that stopped because
you're out of AI credits, say so there too, so a job never finishes in silence.

A note costs **1 credit** to extract (a photo note costs 2 — reading the image
and extracting from it are two actions). Run out and the note is still saved,
with the shortfall spelled out: *"Note saved. You're out of AI credits this
month, so facts weren't extracted."* Add the facts by hand below, or re-run
extraction after the counter resets. See
[AI credits](/docs/guide/ai-credits).

## Add facts and follow-ups by hand

You don't need cloud AI to build a person's profile. When your credits are gone
— or any time you'd rather just type it — use **＋ Add fact** in the Facts
section and
**＋ Add follow-up** in the Follow-ups section. Manual facts have no source note
(nothing to trace back to) and are saved as already-verified, since you entered
them yourself. Everything else in Dhaga — contacts, jobs, contact methods,
relationships, groups — is fully editable by hand too, so the app is completely
usable with no AI at all.

**This is the user's data about third parties**

Facts are extracted from *your* notes about the people you meet. Nothing is
collected silently — a fact only appears because you wrote the note it came
from.

## Editing, deleting, and the cascade

- **Edit or delete a fact** directly if the extraction got something wrong or
  the detail no longer applies.
- **Re-run extraction** on a note (the rotate icon on the note row) if you
  edited it or the first pass missed something — this replaces the note's
  derived facts and follow-ups rather than duplicating them.
- **Delete the source note** and every fact derived from it is tombstoned along
  with it — the receipt guarantees Dhaga knows exactly which facts to remove.
- **Delete the person** and the cascade runs all the way down: notes, facts,
  graph edges, and embeddings all go with them.

The one exception is the receipt note left behind by an import, a card scan, a
QR scan, or a WhatsApp capture: it can't be edited, deleted, or re-run through
extraction. It is not something you wrote — it is the permanent record of how
the contact got into Dhaga in the first place, so it doesn't count toward your
notes either.

Want to add outside context to a person? See
[Enrich from the web](/docs/guide/enrich-from-web).

---

# Search & Ask Dhaga

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/search-and-ask

The ⌘K command palette has two tabs — Search to filter by name, fact, or note, and Ask Dhaga to get a reasoned, receipted answer over your own graph.

Press **⌘K** (Ctrl+K on Windows/Linux) anywhere in the app to open the command
palette. It has two tabs for the two ways you'll look things up.

## Search

The **Search** tab filters your graph by **name, fact, or note**. Type a query
and it matches across all three, with tunable weights so you can lean the
ranking toward names or toward note content.

![The ⌘K command palette on the Search tab with a query typed and matching people listed](/docs/guide/search-palette.png)

## Ask Dhaga

The **Ask Dhaga** tab takes a **natural-language question** and answers it by
reasoning over your own graph — *"get a reasoned answer with receipts."*

![The ⌘K palette on the Ask Dhaga tab, prompting for a natural-language question answered with receipts](/docs/guide/ask-dhaga.png)

Two things make the answers trustworthy:

- **Receipts.** Every answer points back to the notes and people it drew on, so
  you can verify it rather than take it on faith. On a wide screen they sit in a
  side rail next to the answer; on a phone they stack beneath it.
- **No fabrication.** If the answer isn't in your notes or graph, Dhaga says so
  — it will not invent a plausible-sounding answer.

![Ask Dhaga with its source contacts](/docs/guide/ask-dhaga-rail.png)

**Ask Dhaga uses the LLM**

Answering questions runs through Claude. On a self-hosted instance this needs
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or your own LLM provider — see
[Add an LLM provider](/docs/extending/llm-provider)); Search itself works
without it.

---

# Settings & import

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/settings

The Settings page — profile, appearance, billing, 2FA, calendar, suggestions, card-photo storage, voice teaching, API keys — and importing your contacts from a file, a Google or Outlook connect, or your phone.

**`/app/settings`** is where you tune how Dhaga behaves and connect it to the
rest of your tools.

![The Dhaga settings page with its Account, Capture, Calendar, Suggestions, and Import tabs, showing the Account tab's Profile card (editable name and read-only sign-in email) above the Security section](/docs/guide/settings.png)

## What you can configure

Settings is grouped into tabs — pick a tab along the top and its sections sit
beneath it.

- **Account** — your **Profile** (edit your display name; your sign-in email is
  shown read-only and can't be changed here), **Appearance** (the app's colour
  theme and font — see below), **Billing** and plan, **Security**
  (two-factor authentication, 2FA), and **API keys** — personal access tokens for
  the API and the browser extension, and for scripted
  [exports](/docs/self-hosting/deploy#backups--migration). On a hosted instance
  the Billing section also shows a one-line **AI credits** summary — *"3 of 10 AI
  credits used"*. Free accounts have a monthly allowance like any other: **10
  credits a month**. The line only reads *"No monthly AI credits on this plan —
  upgrade to enable AI actions"* if whoever runs the instance has explicitly set
  your allowance to 0, which isn't the normal free-tier state. The full picture
  lives in its own tab, next door.
- **Credits** — your AI-credit ledger: how many are left this month and when they
  reset, a breakdown of where the rest went by kind of action, and a list of your
  most recent AI actions. Credits are charged per action, not per model call: a
  card scan, note, quick-add or draft costs 1; a question to Ask Dhaga or a
  pre-meeting brief costs 2; enriching a contact from the web costs 20. Nightly
  watchlist scans are free — they show in the breakdown marked *Free* rather than
  being hidden. Credits aren't the only gate: enrichment and pre-meeting briefs
  are Pro-and-up features whatever your balance says. Your allowance can be
  raised by whoever runs the instance — a
  promotional month, or credits granted to you after something went wrong on
  their side — and extra credits are only ever *added* on top: what you spent is
  a record and is never rewritten. Full walkthrough:
  [AI credits](/docs/guide/ai-credits). Operators: those controls are the admin
  AI credits screen, documented in
  [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting#instance-wide-ai-credit-controls-appadminai-credits-hostedee).
- **Capture** — **Card photos** (whether the original card image is kept after a
  scan) and **Voice teaching** — a vocabulary manager where you teach Dhaga
  names it keeps mishearing. The fastest way to teach a word is tap-to-fix right
  in the dictation transcript; anything you correct there shows up here.
- **Calendar** — connect Google or Outlook so Dhaga can work against your
  schedule. A new connection reads your **busy times only** — no titles, no
  guests — and writes nothing. Each connection can be **upgraded** on its own,
  from a second consent screen, to also show its events on
  [your calendar](/docs/guide/calendar) and write your follow-ups to a separate
  calendar called **Dhaga** (never your main one). Upgrading is per calendar, and
  the write-out has its own off switch.
- **Suggestions** — the daily reach-out suggestions and email digest that feed
  your Home briefing, a **morning follow-up reminder** email that nudges you
  when you have follow-ups or check-ins waiting, and an opt-in **Confirmations
  digest** email (off by default) that summarises the AI confirmations waiting
  for your review. The same tab holds **Birthdays & anniversaries**: how many
  days ahead a saved date counts as upcoming (0–90, default 7), and an opt-in
  reminder email that arrives that far in advance. **Background job alerts** sits
  alongside them: an opt-in email for when a note extraction or web enrichment
  **fails or is blocked** by your AI budget, at most one every 15 minutes. Runs
  that succeed are not emailed — every job, successful or not, is recorded in
  your notifications, and a run that worked asks nothing of you. Like every email
  preference in Dhaga these start off — the first-run walkthrough stops here so
  you choose, and nothing is switched on for you. It also holds your **Time
  zone** — see below.
- **Import** — bring an existing address book into Dhaga (see below).

**Some sections depend on configuration**

Billing only appears when the instance has Stripe configured, and calendar/
email features need their providers wired up. On a plain self-host several of
these sections are intentionally absent — see [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).

## Appearance

**Account → Appearance** — or the direct link **`/app/settings#appearance`** —
changes how the Dhaga app looks: a **colour theme** and a **font**, both yours
alone. It's also where the first-run walkthrough's settings leg opens — you can
click a theme while the tour is still on screen.

![The Appearance card in the Settings Account tab: a "Colour theme" grid of theme options with three colour swatches each, followed by a Font dropdown and Reset to default button](/docs/guide/settings-appearance.png)

### Pick a theme

Eight themes ship: **Dhaga** (the calm blue-white/midnight default), **Dhaga
Classic** (the original warm paper/charcoal and amber identity), **Monochrome**,
**High contrast**, **Rose**, **Ocean**, **Forest** and **Violet**. Pick one and
the app repaints immediately — there's no Save button on this card.

**A theme changes the colours, not light vs dark**

**Light and dark stay where they always were** — on the toggle in the top bar.
Every theme here ships *both* a light and a dark palette, so whichever you pick,
the toggle keeps doing exactly what it did: a theme decides the hues, the toggle
decides which of its two palettes you see.

![The Dhaga Home briefing rendered under the Monochrome theme — the same metric tiles, sparklines, daily briefing and follow-ups as usual, with every amber accent replaced by neutral greys on a black-and-white ground](/docs/guide/app-theme-monochrome.png)

![The Dhaga Home briefing rendered under the Rose theme — the same layout again, this time on a deep pink-tinted ground with rose accents on the buttons, sparklines and highlighted rows](/docs/guide/app-theme-rose.png)

The list is a fixed set rather than a free colour picker on purpose. Every
theme's palette is contrast-tested in CI on every change — body and secondary text and
accent text against WCAG AA, and control borders against the 3:1 minimum — in
both of its modes. A hand-mixed colour can't be held to that, and unreadable
timestamps are a much worse outcome than a shorter list.

### Pick a font

The **Font** dropdown offers **Geist Pixel** (Dhaga's own display face, and the
default), **System** (your OS's own UI font — downloads nothing), and **Inter**,
**Roboto**, **Open Sans**, **Lato**, **Montserrat** and **Poppins**. The
dropdown and each option render in the face they name, so you can see the
choice before you make it. Nothing is downloaded until you actually open the
list — staying on Geist Pixel costs you no extra font download at all.

### It follows you, and it stops at the app

Your choice is saved **against your account on the server**, not in the browser
— so it's there on your laptop, your phone browser and any machine you sign in
on next, and clearing your browser data doesn't lose it. Because it's stored
server-side, the app arrives already wearing your theme: there's no flash of the
default palette while a page loads.

It applies to **`/app` only**. The public site, this documentation and the blog
keep Dhaga's own colours. That's deliberate rather than an omission — those
pages are pre-rendered and shared with everyone, and making them per-reader
would mean rendering them fresh on every visit and giving up their page speed.

**Reset to default** puts both back: the Dhaga theme and Geist Pixel. It's
greyed out when you're already on both.

## Your time zone

Under **Suggestions**, **Time zone** is the setting that decides where your day
begins and ends. Search for a city or region, or take the **Use detected zone**
shortcut when Dhaga notices your browser disagrees with what's saved — it fills
the box for you and waits; nothing changes until you press Save.

It matters because reminders are about *days*. With it set, a birthday reaches
you on the day it is where **you** are, rather than wherever the server happens
to be, and a reminder you've already had can't arrive again.

**It picks the day, not the hour**

Everything still goes out on one daily run, so the *time* an email lands is set
by the instance, not by your zone. Your time zone decides which **day** a
reminder belongs to — not what time of morning it arrives.

New accounts start on **UTC** until you choose one, so nothing shifts under
anyone who hasn't looked at this yet.

## Import your contacts

The **Import** tab brings an existing address book into Dhaga. Drop a **`.vcf`
(vCard) or CSV** export (Google, LinkedIn, Outlook, iCloud) and it's **parsed in
your browser** — it doesn't get uploaded somewhere to be processed. Where the
instance is configured for it, **one-click Google or Outlook** connectors pull
your contacts in directly, and the **mobile app** can import the contacts already
on your phone. The imported people land in your graph ready to enrich with notes.
See [Importing contacts](/docs/guide/importing-contacts) for the full walkthrough.

---

# Share & invite

Source: https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/share-and-invite

Wrapped turns your graph into a contact-free share card you can post anywhere; Invite friends gives you and a friend a free month of Pro.

![Dhaga's Wrapped share card with a scope picker and reveal-gated names](/docs/guide/wrapped.png)

## Network Wrapped

**`/app/wrapped`** (nav **Wrapped**) is a shareable, year-in-review-style recap of
your networking — "47 people met this month", "strongest cluster: fintech". Every
figure is computed deterministically from your own graph with plain SQL, so
there's no AI cost and nothing to meter. It's part of the core, and works the same
on a self-hosted instance.

- **Pick a scope.** The scope picker recaps a single **event**, or a rolling
  window — **this week**, **this month**, **this quarter**, **this year** (the
  default), or **all time**.
- **Pick a format.** Export the card as a **Post** (landscape), **Square**, or
  **Story** — the aspect ratios for a feed, a grid, or a full-screen story.
- **Share it.** Download the image, copy the public link, or hand off to your
  device's share sheet.

**Names never leave your device unless you choose**

The card is contact-free by construction: it shows aggregate counts and category
superlatives only. The two name-bearing figures — your top company and
most-connected person — stay hidden behind a **Show my names** toggle that reveals
them **in-app, for you only**. They never enter the share token, the link, or the
image, so a card you post leaks nothing about the people in your graph.

## Invite friends

**`/app/referral`** (nav **Invite friends**) is a two-sided referral: share your
link and both you and the friend who joins get a **free month of Pro**. A valid
